method.mechanism: Agent hypothesis: add 0.10 times the difference between the current normalized state and the immediately preceding valid normalized state to the incumbent blended representation. The generated control subtracts that identical difference. Both retain the incumbent context computation and use zero contrast when no immediately preceding valid token exists. The sign comparison tests temporal sharpening against temporal smoothing; it does not by itself identify why either might affect ranking.

proposal.expected_primary_and_slice_effects: Provisional prediction: seed-42 unweighted four-category mean HR@10 exceeds the observed 0.56325 incumbent mean by more than 0.005 and exceeds the opposite-sign control. proposal.falsification_condition: Reject implementation admission if fixed-state sign symmetry, causality, masking or scoring checks fail. If eligible, require the existing independent-seed confirmation rule; failure to reproduce the advantages leaves the ranking hypothesis unsupported. A control advantage contradicts the predicted benefit of temporal sharpening.
